clue.text: Dare bather change into costume that is so worn out?

indicators.note: dressing up in a costume changes how something looks, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone daring a bather to dress up in a costume so shabby it is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change into costume' signals that DAREBATHER is rearranged; 'that is' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth worn so thin that the threads show is shabby and exhausted, so the word also means hackneyed or used up.

clue.text: No right to have attempted to have drawn

indicators.note: no right means the letter for right is to be dropped from the word

parts.note: to have attempted is to have tried

explanation.surface: Having no entitlement to try, and ending level instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn game is one finishing level, with neither side winning.

clue.text: Joseph and I come in to give an answer

indicators.note: the two pieces come in, entering inside the word for giving

parts.note: to render is to give, as in rendering a service
Jo is a short form of Joseph

explanation.surface: Joseph and the speaker arrive to offer a reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort or sharp reply is a response to something said.

clue.text: Donkey goes round by the canyon

indicators.note: the donkey word goes round, enclosing the other piece

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A donkey walks round past the edge of a canyon.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasm is a deep gorge, the same sort of deep rocky drop as a canyon.

clue.text: Chicken found right in the water heater

indicators.note: found in means the letter sits inside the heater word

parts.note: a boiler heats water for a house

explanation.surface: A chicken has turned up inside the hot-water tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A young bird reared for roasting or grilling is sold under that name.

clue.text: Square boy?

parts.note: a London square in Bloomsbury that shares its name with a common boy's given name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' suggests old-fashioned or dull; here it is a London square, Russell Square in Bloomsbury, whose name is also a boy's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The boy's first name is also that of a well-known square in London's Bloomsbury.

clue.text: Lifeless dwelling-place

explanation.definitionFit: Lifeless means dull or without sparkle, and an apartment on one floor is a home.

clue.text: Girl consumes some pilau ravenously

indicators.note: the girl's name eats up some of the following words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A girl wolfs down part of a plate of pilau.
explanation.definitionFit: A common woman's given name, as for a girl.

clue.text: One who comes into property without inheriting it

definitions.text: One who comes into property without inheriting it

parts.words: One who comes into property without inheriting it
parts.note: coming into property usually means inheriting it; here it is literal, walking onto land without leave

explanation.walkthrough: 'comes into property' is the idiom for inheriting, but here it means physically entering land.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder on private land enters someone's property without any right to be there.

clue.text: Examine the pay-desk

explanation.definitionFit: To inspect something is to look it over, and the till in a supermarket where you pay is also named so.

clue.text: Have the benefit of experience?

explanation.definitionFit: To possess and profit from something, as one does good health, and to undergo or relish an occasion.

clue.text: Hops in here to dry

parts.note: hops suggests jumping in, but means the bitter flowers used in brewing, dried in a kiln building

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hops' reads as a verb of jumping; it is the plant used to flavour beer, dried in a kiln building found in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln building with a cowled roof, used in Kent for drying the flowers that flavour beer.

clue.text: Unruly Sid loves to break up

indicators.note: unruly letters are disorderly and get rearranged

explanation.surface: Sid's wild romances keep ending in splits.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissolve a partnership or parliament is to end it or disband it.

clue.text: Vice of leader in temporary quarters

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the quarters word

parts.note: a camp is a temporary place to stay
the leader of a word is its first letter; here the first letter of leader itself

explanation.surface: A head of some wickedness found in a makeshift base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vice' looks like wickedness; it is the gripping tool on a workbench.
explanation.definitionFit: A bench vice and a clamp are both tools that grip and hold work tight.

clue.text: Clergy on board shaken after a meal

indicators.note: one piece sits on top of the other, as cloth lies on a table

parts.note: a table is a board, as in bed and board
the cloth is a collective term for the clergy

explanation.surface: Churchmen at a dinner table are rattled once the meal is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the clergy word on the board word, as a cloth is laid on a table.
explanation.definitionFit: The linen covering spread over a dining table is shaken out to remove crumbs after eating.

clue.text: Accountant who listens?

explanation.definitionFit: A person checking a firm's books is one meaning; a hearer or listener, from the Latin for hear, is the other.

clue.text: Test out cake in a court of justice

indicators.note: the cake goes in, inside the test word

parts.note: a trial is a test run, trying something out
a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: Trying out a cake at a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: A body set up to judge disputes or claims acts as a court.

clue.text: She has her pride

parts.note: pride reads as self-respect, but is the collective word for a group of big cats

explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' suggests self-esteem; it is a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A female big cat lives in a group of lions, called a pride.

clue.text: Not hard cash presumably

parts.note: hard cash means coins and notes; read literally, cash that is not hard is money earned without effort

explanation.walkthrough: 'hard cash' is the idiom for actual money; taking 'hard' as difficult gives money that comes without effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Money got with little effort is the opposite of hard-earned income.

clue.text: Crazy ruling accepting king who is lying in wait

indicators.note: the scrambled word accepts, taking in, the king letter

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A mad decision takes in a monarch who is hiding in ambush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' rearranges RULING into LURING, which 'accepting' wraps round K.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiding out of sight ready to pounce describes one skulking in ambush.

clue.text: It hardly moves down the mountain

definitions.text: It hardly moves down the mountain

parts.words: It hardly moves down the mountain
parts.note: a mass of ice creeping downhill at a barely noticeable pace

explanation.definitionFit: A river of ice flows downhill so slowly the movement is barely visible.

clue.text: Entertainer tries at diversification

indicators.note: diversifying the letters means spreading them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A performer has a go at branching out.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional performer, such as a singer or dancer, on stage.

clue.text: Reach a church before I take the first lady

indicators.note: in a down clue before means placed above, so the church comes first

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: Arriving at church before the speaker escorts the original woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain a goal is to get to it, to reach it.

clue.text: Shy upturned rodent

parts.note: coy means shy or bashful
the word up turned around gives PU

explanation.surface: A timid creature with its nose in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upturned' is UP turned back, giving PU.
explanation.definitionFit: A large South American water-dwelling animal of the rat family, farmed for fur.

clue.text: Submit produce

explanation.definitionFit: To give in or surrender, and the crop or output of land or investment.

clue.text: Cyst that hero Martin was disguising

indicators.note: the words were covering up the answer, hiding it inside them

explanation.surface: A heroic man named Martin concealed a growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatty deposit or swelling, particularly a sebaceous cyst or a lesion in an artery wall.

clue.text: Out Dora and I set

indicators.note: out signals letters knocked out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Dora and the speaker are ready to go out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is a noun: a broadcasting receiver, as in a television or wireless set.
explanation.definitionFit: A wireless receiver is a piece of equipment, a set, picking up broadcasts.

clue.text: Able to go where one likes at no charge

definitions.text: Able to go where one likes

explanation.definitionFit: Unconfined and at liberty, and costing nothing, gratis.

clue.text: Worker having force

explanation.definitionFit: A factory hand is a worker, and a rule in effect is in operation, valid.

clue.text: He gives Spaniard alternative

parts.note: Don is a Spanish title for a gentleman
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman offering another option.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactor or blood giver is someone who gives.

clue.text: Nasty side of the park?

explanation.definitionFit: Mr Hyde is the evil alter ego of Dr Jekyll in Stevenson's tale, and Hyde Park is a large royal park in central London.

clue.text: Unexceptionally devoted as a printer to his craft?

definitions.text: devoted as a printer to his craft

explanation.definitionFit: Behaving typically, as expected, and loyal to printing type, as a printer would be.
